minutes.summary: The board accepted a de minimis sign change and heard a pre-submittal for a used car lot on Summer Street, where it is unclear whether the zoning permit allows 20 or 50 cars. The car lot and bond matters were carried to January 8.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board carried the Stone Farms bond decision to January 8, with staff to request an estimate from the town's engineer and consult the fire department.
The Summer Street used car lot request was carried to January 8; staff are to ask the Zoning Board whether the permit allows 20 or 50 cars.
The board accepted a de minimis change to a sign location at 400 Electric Avenue, and nominated members to capital planning and the school building committee.
The board tabled the definitions and use table, and held January 29 as a possible workshop date on it.
The board heard a proposed marijuana bylaw change in discussion, with no vote recorded.

why_it_matters: The Stone Farms bond is the cash the town holds to make sure the subdivision's roads and utilities are finished, so how much is released or held back affects whether the town or the developer pays for any unfinished work.

The 20-versus-50 car question on Summer Street, and the rewrite of the use table and marijuana bylaw, set what can be built or operated where, and changes to zoning bylaws can come to Town Meeting for a vote.
watch_next: January 8: the Planning Board returns to the Summer Street used car lot and the Stone Farms bond.
January 29: held as a possible workshop on the definitions and use table.
